data.title: Internal Detail Disclosed in Published Document Metadata
data.summary: Documents published on the website retained metadata disclosing usernames, internal file paths, software versions and printer and server names, providing an attacker with the naming conventions needed for targeted attacks.
data.description:
Office documents and PDFs record their own production: the account that created them, the template path, the software and version, revision history, and sometimes the network path or printer used.

Collected across a set of published documents, this yields the organisation's username format — which is exactly what is needed to turn a list of employee names into a list of valid accounts for spraying — together with internal server names, directory structures and a view of which software versions are deployed.

Images carry the equivalent: camera and device identifiers, and sometimes GPS coordinates, which matter for physical reconnaissance of sites that are not publicly listed.
data.recommendation:
* Strip metadata as a mandatory step before publishing any document or image.
* Automate it in the publication pipeline rather than relying on the author.
* Audit documents already published and republish cleaned versions.
* Prefer exporting to PDF with metadata removal enabled over converting in place.
data.short_recommendation: Strip metadata from documents before publication.
